text:
maria: Heads-up — after last night's label rollout in eu-west1 we started seeing a big spike in Pending GPU pods. Lots of evictions and backfill noise. Anyone watching?
kevin: Yup. Evict count +240 in the last hour in eu-west1b. Dashboard shows many pods Pending with nodeAffinity for gpu-type=v100 and failing to land.
sam: Seeing scheduler rejections. A node taint (gpu-rollout=true:NoSchedule) was applied by the rollout job; warm-pool nodes didn't get the new gpu-tier label so they aren't matching affinity.
jen: Oncall, can you temporarily relax the taint for warm-pool while we triage? We avoid broad rollbacks but need immediate relief.
infra-bot: [alert] 1717032120 - automated-rollout: applied taint gpu-rollout=true to 18 nodes in eu-west1b as part of label rollout job.
maria: can someone paste a kubectl describe of a representative Pending pod?
kevin: 
```
Name:         train-worker-5
Namespace:    p-ml
Node:         <none>
Labels:       app=train
Annotations:  <none>
Status:       Pending
Events:
  Type     Reason            Age    From               Message
  ----     ------            ----   ----               -------
  Warning  FailedScheduling  2m     default-scheduler  0/18 nodes are available: 18 node(s) had taint {gpu-rollout=true:NoSchedule}.
```

sam: scheduler logs: "pod p-ml/train-worker-5 unschedulable: TaintToleration mismatch; nodeAffinity requires gpu-tier=compact" — TL;DR labels + taints out of sync with warm nodes. Also noticed many pods have strict podTopologySpread across zones, which is making packing worse (can't consolidate into fewer nodes).
jen: Proposed immediate steps:
- add toleration to canary workloads via admission patch for the next hour
- run a small controlled drain on tainted nodes to migrate long-running batch jobs into warm-pool nodes once labels fixed
- add an automated pre-check in rollout job to ensure warm-pool label parity before applying taint
maria: +1. Also add a quick script to detect when label rollout applies taints but available nodes for the affinity set are < 25% capacity — that should block taint application.
kevin: Quick diagnostic command to map labels/taints vs allocs: 
```
kubectl get nodes -l gpu-tier=compact -o wide && kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}:{.spec.taints}\n'
```

sam: I'm patching the canary to include toleration + controlled nodeSelector fallback. Running now.
sam: Patch applied, canary pods rescheduled to warm-pool, eviction rate down from 240/hr -> ~12/hr. Looks like toleration helped.
jen: Good. Can someone open a postmortem ticket and add the checklist we discussed? I'll own the rollout job change.
maria: I'll file the ticket and include the scheduler snippets + k8s audit for the rollout time. Also adding an item to check podTopologySpread configs for strict spread that amplifies fragmentation.
deploy-bot: Rollout job completed: labels applied to 3 zones; taint applied as part of job (see audit).
maria: Thanks everyone. Follow-up: we shouldn't roll labels+taints in a single automated step until the parity check is in place. :thumbsup:
kevin: Agreed. Will add a quick metric alert for Pending GPU pods correlated with "taint applied" events.
jen: I'll PR the rollout job change this afternoon.
infra-bot: NOTE: created incident ticket INC-2026-1482 for investigation (linked in ticket).
